note: Pictures: none. loadMetrics.reading: First paint and the page itself do not move: first contentful paint 632 to 640 ms on the phone and 232 to 256 ms (base) against 212 to 248 ms (head) on the desktop; DOM content loaded the same within 10 ms; layout shift about 0. Requests are equal on the phone (60) and two fewer on the desktop (172 against 174; the head mounts no flat preview for a live box, the cause of the two was not traced). Transfer varies from run to run on both sides by the random painting the hero shows (the hero picks one of several 100 to 750 KB paintings): base 1194 to 1470 KB, head 1144 to 1294 KB on the phone; base 8611 to 9450 KB, head 9073 to 9484 KB on the desktop, so the sides overlap. The phone LCP is the hero painting on a slow network (6.4 to 6.7 s on both sides, median 6600 base, 6528 head): the live boxes add none to it.

measureJson.what: frame gaps of the page interactions at 1440x900 and 390x844 (no CPU slowdown): hero idle incl. a painting change, a card open and close, scroll to the blocks, open the shelf and watching layers, hover, open a book and a video, close
measureJson.fixedInThisTask: At 390x844 the watching layer was opened by clicking the second block's button while the block was far below the screen (a visitor cannot do that: the box scenes are prepared when their block comes within 240 px of the screen, R55.2). The wall then gave up to its plain grid and the next step (hover across the wall canvas) read nothing. The step now scrolls the watching block into view and waits 1.5 s, as a visitor would; the same file runs on the base.
measureJson.firstTryWithTheOlderFile: head, three runs: runs 1 and 3 clean; run 2 had frames of 300 ms (1440, scroll to the blocks), 150 ms (1440, open the reading layer) and 100 ms (390, close reading and open watching), the only frames over 20 ms in 6 runs of that file; base 0 of 3. Not reproduced in the 3 runs of the corrected file; the machine was shared at the time. Recorded here, not explained.
measureJson.reading: With the corrected file: 24 steps per run, no frame over 20 ms, worst gap 16.8 ms, on both sides in all three runs.

reading: Corrected after the fix round (the first reading credited the two fewer desktop requests to "no flat preview for a live box", which was not so: the server and hydration renders still mounted both flat previews, and a live visitor loaded the mini wall thumbnails, 14 at 1440x900 and 12 on the phone). Now a live visitor mounts none (box-picture.ts): the phone makes 48 requests against the base 60 and the desktop 158 against 173 to 174, the 12 (phone) to 16 (desktop) thumbnails (mqdefault) of the flat mini wall; scripts/audit/live-thumbs.json counts 0 flat-wall thumbnails for a live visitor at 1440x900 and on the phone (and 16 with ?nogl=1, the control). Timings, 3 runs each, alternated, a shared machine: first contentful paint 624 to 676 ms (head) against 640 to 764 ms (base, second sample; 628 to 632 in the first) on the phone and 232 to 252 against 240 to 260 on the desktop; DOM content loaded the same within about 40 ms; layout shift about 0; largest contentful paint 6204 to 6516 ms (head) against 6648 to 6680 ms (base second sample; 6404 to 6696 first) on the phone and 540 to 576 ms against 656 to 676 ms (second sample; 636 to 676 first) on the desktop. The first head sample showed the desktop largest contentful paint 30 to 50 ms later than the base (676 to 708 ms against 636 to 676 ms, every head run at or above every base run), which the review asked the record to state; it does not repeat after the fix (the head is now 80 to 130 ms earlier), so the likely reading is that the two flat previews mounting during hydration (and their images) cost the head that time, and no longer do; not traced further. Transfer is dominated by the random hero painting (8.3 to 10.4 MB on the desktop, 1.1 to 1.9 MB on the phone on both sides, ranges overlapping). One difference that remains by design: a visitor whose scene fails or has no WebGL now sees the dark ground for the few frames before the flat preview mounts, and the flat wall thumbnails load then, at network speed, instead of from the first paint.
